'''Ngandi''' is an extinct [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]] of the [[Wilton River]], [[Northern Territory]]. It is closely related to [[Nunggubuyu language|Nunggubuyu]].

In 2017 the last fluent speaker of Ngandi, Cherry Wulumirr Daniels, began teaching the language to younger people at [[Ngukurr]].<ref name="news">{{Cite news|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-04-16/future-of-endangered-ngandi-language-rests-with-youth/8446414|title=Future of endangered Indigenous language rests with youth|last=James|first=Felicity|date=2017-04-16|work=ABC News|access-date=2018-01-21|language=en-AU}}</ref> She died in 2019.<ref name="monash">{{cite web |title=Preserving Indigenous languages |url=https://lens.monash.edu/@monash-life/2019/10/27/1377046/preserving-indigenous-languages |website=Monash Life |date=27 October 2019 |publisher=Monash University |access-date=12 August 2020}}</ref><ref name="yugul">{{cite web |date=24 April 2019 |title=Cherry Wulumirr Daniels laid to rest |url=https://yugulmangicom.wordpress.com/2019/04/24/cherry-wulumirr-daniels-laid-to-rest/ |access-date=12 August 2020 |website=Yugul Mangi Development Aboriginal Corporation}}</ref>
